references.text: Emphasizes that what enters the mouth and then leaves the body is not what defiles a person.
Peter receives a vision teaching him that no food is inherently unclean, which corresponds with Jesus' teaching that it is not what enters the mouth that makes a person unclean.
Peter refers to the vision he had, confirming Jesus' teaching that it is not food that defiles a person.
Paulus mentions that food is for the stomach and the stomach for food, but God will destroy both, which resonates with Jesus' point that food itself is not what defiles.
